resolutions.evidence:
**Ran** in a mktemp copy of 22113ac (pi 1.5.2, faux provider, no model call; removed afterwards). Each run used a probe applying decision 2's budget and decision 9's cache-hit whole-block fit, at pi's default compaction settings unless noted. Faux model calls answered the summarisation request.

| Window | Conversation (tokens) | Item | Step | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 40,960 | 9,383 | 12,800 | 3,000 | Request 1 appended the block (budget 15,193 tokens). No `session_before_compact`, no compaction entry. Request 2 estimated 12,385 with a budget of 12,191, so the block was dropped by decision 9's fit with no compaction involved |
| 262,144 | 190,983 | 50,000 | 7,000 | `session_before_compact` threshold before step 2 (22 messages summarised), then `session_compact`. The next request estimated 24,189 with a budget of 221,571, and the cached block was appended again |
| 1,000,000 | 931,383 | 50,000 | 6,000 | The same, with 58 messages summarised. The next request estimated 22,900, and the block was appended again |
| 40,960 with `keepRecentTokens` 2,000 | 9,383 | 12,800 | 3,000 | Compacted, and the cached block was appended again |

**Read in pi 1.5.2:**
- `dist/core/compaction/compaction.js` L56: `keepRecentTokens: 20000`.
- `compaction.js` L334-360: `findCutPoint` keeps from the first message when the entries total less than `keepRecentTokens`.
- `compaction.js` L642-643: `prepareCompaction` returns `undefined` when there is nothing to summarise.
- `dist/core/agent-session.js` L2629-2631: `_runAutoCompaction` returns false without compacting when there is no preparation.
- `docs/compaction.md` L45 and L435.

`design.md` L275 already states that the block's bytes change only when the block is dropped, each change costing one cache rewrite.
resolutions.rationale:
The finding's mechanism does not happen at pi's defaults on any of Joel's three windows. I measured it, and its recommended sentence would add a false claim, so it must not be applied.

**On the 40,960-token model,** the case it names never compacts. pi's default `keepRecentTokens` of 20,000 is larger than any conversation short enough for a 12,800-token item to fit, so pi finds nothing to summarise and returns without compacting. The block is gone at the next step only because decision 9's cache-hit fit drops it once the step has shrunk the budget. That is documented behaviour (decision 9 cache hit, step 3; L275), and no compaction is involved.

**On the 262,144- and 1,000,000-token windows,** recall did cause a compaction. The compaction then freed most of the conversation, and the cached block fitted again and was re-appended for the rest of the turn. So the Risks row's "Archived outputs stay recallable across a compaction" holds within the turn as well.

**What the finding's location does expose** is a real defect: the Risks row's 40,960-token bullet and decision 2's measured cases are wrong at pi's defaults. That is a separate finding I raise as michael-s3-r6-M1.

I raise this while verifying CRIT-R6-1, in the row it names. Every compaction measurement I put into decision 2, in rounds 1, 3 and 4, ran with `keepRecentTokens` 2,000 instead of pi's default 20,000, and the design never records that. That is a provenance defect in my own measurements.

At the defaults:
- the 20,000- and 40,960-token cases compact nothing;
- the Risks row's "a compaction follows nearly every recall of a large item there", my round-2 arithmetic, is false.

pi compacts only when there is something to summarise. That needs the persisted conversation, step included, to reach `keepRecentTokens`. On the 40,960-token model that leaves recall only a few thousand tokens. So a large item there cannot cause a recall-caused compaction at defaults; decision 9 drops its block at the next step instead.

The 262,144 and 1,000,000 bullets stand, because near those thresholds the conversation is far above 20,000. The spec and the proposal say only "may" or "can", so they stand too.

**Why I rate it major.** It is the same class and the same row as R2-1, R3-1 and R4-1: the record of an owner-accepted, persisted outcome. The PL2 carry-forward would tell Joel a false premise about his small-window model. The ADR in the docs queue would record measurements that no one could reproduce at defaults. It overstates the risk rather than understating it, which standard §6 also cuts.

**Churn check.** The previous round patched nothing. Reverting round 4's or round 3's wording would not fix the missing setting or the round-2 bullet, so this is not churn.
resolutions.required_change:
Change wording only, in `design.md`. Change no mechanism, no spec text, no proposal text, and do not edit `owner-rulings.md`.

**1. Decision 2, "The measured case" (L126).**

(a) Insert this precondition right after the title's parenthetical setup, citing pi 1.5.2 and Michael's Stage 3 round 6 probe:

> "pi compacts only when there is something to summarise. `prepareCompaction` returns nothing, and `_runAutoCompaction` returns without compacting, when the persisted conversation since the last compaction totals less than `keepRecentTokens`, which defaults to 20,000 (`compaction.js` L56, L334-360, L642-643; `agent-session.js` L2629-2631). So a recall-caused compaction needs that conversation, the step included, to reach `keepRecentTokens`. The block itself is not persisted and does not count."

(b) State once that every measurement in this paragraph (the 20,000-token case and both 40,960-token cases from rounds 3 and 4) set `keepRecentTokens` to 2,000, and that at pi's default of 20,000 those cases compact nothing.

(c) Add the measurements at pi's defaults:

> "At pi's default compaction settings (round 6 probe):
> - a 40,960-token window, a 9,383-token conversation, a 12,800-token item and a 3,000-token step: the item was recalled and nothing was compacted. The next step dropped the block by decision 9's cache-hit fit.
> - a 262,144-token window, a 190,983-token conversation, a 50,000-token item and a 7,000-token step: pi compacted before step 2, and the cached block fitted again and was appended for the rest of the turn.
> - a 1,000,000-token window, a 931,383-token conversation, a 50,000-token item and a 6,000-token step: the same."

Keep the paragraph's other sentences (`compaction.enabled`, `decisionThreshold`, `reserveTokens`) and add only the `keepRecentTokens` 2,000 qualifier to their measurements.

**2. The Risks / Trade-offs row beginning "A recall that fills most of its budget" (L395).**

In its 40,960-token bullet, replace everything after "(threshold 24,576):" with:

> "at pi's default `keepRecentTokens` of 20,000, a large item cannot cause one: a conversation short enough for it to fit has nothing for pi to summarise, so pi does not compact, and decision 9 drops the block at the next step instead. A recall-caused compaction there needs the conversation, with the step, to reach 20,000 tokens, which leaves recall only a few thousand tokens. With `keepRecentTokens` lowered, one large item is enough again (decision 2)."

Extend the row's last sentence to read:

> "Archived outputs stay recallable across a compaction, because hydration reads the whole branch (D5). Within the same turn, the cached block is appended again once the compaction frees room for it, as measured on the 262,144- and 1,000,000-token windows (decision 2)."

Leave the 1,000,000 and 262,144 bullets as they are.

settled_findings:
critic-r6-CRIT-R6-1 (contested). Measured at pi's defaults (pi 1.5.2, round 6 probe):
- On the 40,960-token model, a large-item recall causes no compaction, because there is nothing to summarise under `keepRecentTokens` 20,000. The block drops at the next step by decision 9's documented cache-hit fit.
- On the 262,144- and 1,000,000-token windows, the compaction recall causes frees room, and the cached block is appended again within the turn.

Do not reopen unless decision 9's cache-hit rule, decision 4's token, or the session_compact hydration changes.

critic-r2-CRIT-R2-2 (fixed). Decision 13's setup check (6) reads only the pre-probe snapshots of prompt 2's requests and of prompt 3's first request. This was measured: false on a correct run, true when nothing was archived. Do not reopen unless decision 13's session sequence or observation changes.

critic-r1-CRIT-2 (minor, declined). The notice can name the wrong field after slow auth or a transient provider error. pi's own `errorMessage` is in the same notice, and ruling 1's rule-over-facts approach stands. Do not reopen unless decision 7's template or table changes.

critic-r1-CRIT-3 (minor, declined). The marker guard guarantees exactly one literal opening and one literal closing marker, and the spec tests that. Variants differing in case or whitespace are not rewritten. The role move is T13 and goes to Joel at PL2 under ruling 11. Do not reopen unless decision 10's guard changes.

structural-r1-STR-1 (minor, contested). Measured: a lone `.mjs` file in `additionalExtensionPaths` loads, in the order given and before `extensionFactories`, and its `context_with_system` handler runs first. It was re-measured with real taiknr between the two probes. Evidence: `michael-resolve-s2.json` COMP-4. Do not reopen unless decision 13's observation mechanism changes.

structural-r1-STR-2 (minor, declined at Stage 3). The hanging-fetch stub and the test provider registration need one home. Stage 5 holds `tasks.md` to naming it. Do not reopen at Stage 3 or 4 unless decision 12 or the guard's row changes.

structural-r2-STR-1 (minor, declined). The extension-packaging delta's "(design.md Decision 6)" is the living spec's L43 citation, restated verbatim as a MODIFIED delta requires. Do not reopen unless the delta's scenario text changes.

PL2 carry-forward, for the conductor and not a finding. Name these corrections to the premises under Joel's ruling (a) to him at PL2, alongside ruling 11's request-time-redactor item:
- The exposure is as wide as the recalled block, on windows where the conversation near the threshold exceeds pi's `keepRecentTokens` (critic-r2-CRIT-R2-1). On his 40,960-token model at pi's defaults, a large-item recall cannot cause a compaction, and only a few thousand tokens of recall can; this replaces round 2's "nearly every recall" (michael-s3-r6-M1).
- `reserveTokens` is not a lever for this case (critic-r3-CRIT-R3-1).
- pi's `compaction.enabled: false` avoids the case only by turning off all of pi's automatic compaction (critic-r4-CRIT-R4-1).
